questiontext.text: Which set contains the three infrastructure pillars introduced in the lecture?

generalfeedback.text: Compute executes workloads, storage retains data, and networking connects components. The other choices name tools, environments, or application-level concerns.

questiontext.text: Which statement best describes a declarative infrastructure definition?

generalfeedback.text: A declarative definition expresses the intended state. The tool determines the required operations from that definition and the current state. Declarative syntax does not mean every operation is independent or can run concurrently.

answer.text: It records every command an administrator previously executed.
It specifies the exact order of all API calls that a tool must make.
It describes the desired state, while a tool works out how to reach it.
It guarantees that every operation can run in parallel.

questiontext.text: An automation run has successfully reached the desired state. Its inputs and the relevant external state then remain unchanged. What should a second idempotent run do?

generalfeedback.text: Once the declaration is satisfied, repeating the operation under unchanged conditions should not further alter the managed state. Checking state is compatible with idempotence; duplicating or needlessly rebuilding resources is not required.

answer.text: Leave the managed state unchanged because it already satisfies the declaration.
Recreate all resources to prove they can be recreated.
Skip checking the current state and report success.
Add another copy of each declared resource.

questiontext.text: A team moves from managing virtual machines under IaaS to a managed application platform under PaaS. Which responsibility would typically move towards the provider?

generalfeedback.text: PaaS typically transfers more operating-system and runtime-platform maintenance to the provider. The exact responsibility boundary depends on the service. The team still owns its application requirements and code.

answer.text: Maintaining more of the underlying operating system and runtime platform

name.text: L1 Q5 Why keep infrastructure definitions in Git

questiontext.text: Give two benefits of version-controlling infrastructure definitions beyond simply having a backup copy. Explain how each benefit helps a team deliver changes reliably.

graderinfo.text:
Award 1 mark each for two benefits connected to reliable delivery, for example:

  • A reviewable change history helps identify what changed, who changed it, and why.
  • Pull requests and review help catch mistakes before applying changes.
  • Automated validation can run against proposed configuration changes.
  • A shared definition reduces undocumented manual differences between environments.
  • A known earlier definition helps investigate or plan recovery from a bad change.

Do not award a separate benefit for “having another copy.” Reverting a Git commit does not by itself restore deleted data or guarantee a safe infrastructure rollback.

questiontext.text: Two servers were created from the same definition. An administrator later changes a setting manually on only one server. Explain what configuration drift means in this situation and describe one way to detect or reconcile it.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: Actual managed configuration has diverged from its declared or intended state; the manually changed server now differs from that baseline.
  • 1 mark: Compare actual state with the definition, for example through a plan, configuration inspection, or a configuration-management run. Investigate whether the manual change is legitimate, then either update the reviewed declaration or reapply the intended configuration.

name.text: L1 Q7 Mutable and immutable infrastructure

questiontext.text: A server needs a new operating-system configuration. Contrast an in-place mutable update with an immutable replacement. Explain what must happen to persistent application data when using the replacement approach.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: Mutable updates modify the existing server; immutable updates create a replacement from a newly prepared definition or image and switch the workload to it.
  • 1 mark: Preserve persistent data separately or use a tested backup/migration/restore procedure before retiring the old server. Replacement must not discard the only copy of application data.

name.text: L1 Q8 Tool responsibilities in demo 01

questiontext.text: In demo-01, main.tf creates an EC2 instance and writes an Ansible inventory; playbook.yml installs and configures Nginx. Explain the distinct responsibilities of Terraform and Ansible in this workflow.

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: In this demo, Terraform defines and provisions AWS resources and produces connection information, including the inventory.
  • 1 mark: Ansible connects to the target and manages software, files, and service configuration inside the operating system.

These are the roles of the tools in this particular workflow, not an assertion that Ansible cannot manage cloud resources. demo-03a demonstrates that it can.

name.text: L1 Q9 Dependencies and generated inventory

questiontext.text:
Consider these excerpts from demo-01/main.tf:

# Within aws_instance.server
key_name               = aws_key_pair.main_key.key_name
vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.main_security_group.id]

# Within the Terraform-generated inventory template
ansible_host: ${aws_instance.server.public_ip}
  1. Identify the two resources that the instance references and explain what those references tell Terraform about dependency ordering. (2 marks)
  2. Explain why generating ansible_host from the instance output is more reliable than copying an IP address into a separate inventory by hand. Include what must happen to the inventory when a replacement instance receives a new public IP. (2 marks)

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: aws_key_pair.main_key is referenced for the instance's SSH key-pair name.
  • 1 mark: aws_security_group.main_security_group is referenced for the attached security-group ID. Both resource references contribute implicit dependencies, so Terraform must obtain the required resource values before completing the dependent operation. Moving blocks up or down the file is not the dependency mechanism.
  • 1 mark: Using aws_instance.server.public_ip connects the inventory to the provisioned instance's actual output and avoids a separately maintained, potentially stale IP address.
  • 1 mark: Apply/regenerate the inventory after replacement and use that updated inventory for Ansible. A previously copied inventory does not update itself simply because a new instance exists.

Technical reference: Terraform references and dependencies.

name.text: L1 Q10 Predicting a repeated run

questiontext.text:
The following is a shortened version of tasks in demo-01/playbook.yml:

- name: Install nginx
  apt:
    name: nginx
    state: present

- name: Create custom index.html
  copy:
    content: "Course homepage\n"
    dest: /var/www/html/index.html

- name: Start and enable nginx
  systemd:
    name: nginx
    state: started
    enabled: yes

Assume the first run succeeds and all relevant inputs remain unchanged.

  1. Predict the effect of a second run on the package, file, and service. Explain why this illustrates idempotence. (2 marks)
  2. Someone then manually changes the contents of index.html. What should the next run do, and why? (2 marks)

graderinfo.text:
• 1 mark: The installed package remains present; the matching file does not need rewriting; a running and enabled service remains in that state.
  • 1 mark: This is idempotence: once the requested state is reached, repetition with unchanged relevant inputs does not produce additional managed-state changes. The shown state: present does not mean “upgrade to whatever version is newest.”
  • 1 mark: A manual edit makes the managed file differ from the declared content, so the next successful copy task restores the declared contents.
  • 1 mark: The restoration reconciles drift against the declaration. It does not require replacing the whole server or reinstalling Nginx.
